audit.whatIsWrong: The early lane was explained as Zoe poking 'at a range you can't yet answer'. Paddle Star! is 800 and Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 800; Aurora's Q is 900. She is not out-ranged.
audit.why: 52.48% over 909 games at 5.5/10. Zoe owns levels 1-2 for a different reason: one bubble is a kill. Sleep lowers your magic resist and the first source of damage that breaks it is doubled, so the threat is a setup landing, not a range deficit — which changes the instruction from 'stand further back' to 'keep a minion between you and the brush'.
audit.corrected: early, spikes[0].text, phases[0..1].why and wants.foe[2] now state the real ranges and the sleep mechanic.

audit.whatIsWrong: Portal Jump is described as 'built more for roaming and picks' in both spikes[1].text and mid.
audit.why: Riot's text: blink to a nearby position for 1 second, then blink back — 575 range on an 11/8/5s cooldown. It is not a roaming ultimate; it is a short, near-permanent blink she uses to extend her effective bubble range and to dodge. The correct level-6 read is 'she gains reach', not 'her ultimate does not matter in lane'.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and mid rebuilt around the 575 blink, the 1 second, and the 11s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] says her combo comes 'from stealth'. Zoe has no stealth — the threat is a bubble thrown from brush. Separately, nothing anywhere mentioned that sleep REDUCES MAGIC RESIST and that the first damage breaking it is doubled, which is the entire reason one bubble kills.
audit.why: Those two facts change what you buy and how you stand: magic resist is devalued while asleep, so the answer is body-blocking with minions and not standing in bubble lines, not stacking MR. The brief's missing-interactions file flags the resistance point directly.
audit.corrected: whys[0], whys[1], report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, tradeBad and dosFull[0].d now carry the sleep mechanic with its 18s cooldown.

audit.why: Defect item 3. Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18/17/16/15/14 at 800, Paddle Star! 8.5s to 6.5s, Portal Jump 11/8/5.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three, and with the fact that Portal Jump is effectively always available.

audit.whatIsWrong: PRONOUNS. Zoe is female per champ-gender.js, but the full layer calls her 'he/his' in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, ahead, loading, dosFull[0].t, dontsFull[0].t, dontsFull[1].t, report[0].t, report[3].t and report[11].t.
audit.why: Defect item 1 — the template was written for a male enemy and only the name was swapped.
audit.corrected: Every one of those fields fixed, in most cases while also grounding the sentence in Zoe's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every phases[N].side read 'Skill' while win[] and the packet both read Zoe, Zoe, then Aurora for five rows, and phases[0..1].why described Aurora winning the two Zoe rows.
audit.why: Packet and content agree; the sides were stale and the first two whys contradicted the verdict.
audit.corrected: All seven sides aligned as one group, phases[0..1].rating dropped to 4/10, and both whys rewritten to Zoe verdicts grounded in the bubble and Paddle Star!.

notes: 1) MISGENDERING was the headline defect here: Zoe is female per champ-gender.js and twelve full-layer fields called her he/his. All twelve are fixed. Because those strings are the shared Aurora template, the same misgendering is near-certain on aurora's other female matchups (ahri, akali, anivia, annie, cassiopeia, diana, irelia, karma, katarina, leblanc, lissandra, lux, mel, naafiri, neeko, orianna, qiyana, syndra, taliyah, vex) — worth a lint pass across the champion, not just this file. 2) All three packet 'suspect names' are FALSE POSITIVES: Sleepy Trouble Bubble, Paddle Star! and Portal Jump are all correct (the flags are just the trailing '!' and the '-R' suffix). The sentences around two of them were still wrong: Paddle Star! is 800 against Aurora's 900, so 'a range you can't yet answer' is false, and Portal Jump is a 575 one-second blink on 11/8/5, not a roaming ultimate. 3) 'Q Twin Drift' appears again in spikes[0].text and was removed rather than guessed — see the other files in this slice. 4) I did not write any resistance-stacking advice against sleep beyond what Riot's text states (sleep reduces magic resist, first damage doubled up to a cap); the missing-interactions 'resistances-invalidated' rule is consistent with that text, so it was safe to use here.
